title: The Best Angle Grinders of 2026
intro: The best angle grinder for most people in 2026 is the DeWalt DWE402 — an 11-amp corded paddle-switch grinder with a 11,000 RPM motor, a safety lock-off paddle, and DeWalt's three-year limited warranty that covers the widest range of grinding, cutting, and surface prep tasks. Milwaukee M18 FUEL owners who want cordless performance without giving up professional capability should go straight to the 2880-20. Budget cordless buyers on the Ryobi ONE+ platform will find the PCL445B gets the work done, and the Makita GA4534 is the corded pick for anyone who wants the lightest possible tool at 6 amps.

picks.name: DeWalt DWE402 11-Amp Corded Angle Grinder
picks.summary: The DWE402 covers professional grinding, cutting, and surface prep on a corded platform with no battery management overhead. Its 11-amp motor reaches 11,000 RPM — the same ceiling as the lighter Makita — and the paddle switch with safety lock-off is the industry standard for accidental-start prevention. At 4.6 lbs over 12 inches, it is a manageable one-hand or two-hand tool that fits into both fabrication shops and job sites. DeWalt's three-year limited warranty with a one-year free service guarantee backs the investment.
pros: 11-amp motor at 11,000 RPM handles grinding, cutting discs, wire cups, and flap discs
Paddle switch with safety lock-off reduces accidental starts
Three-year limited warranty plus one-year free service — the strongest coverage here
Universal 5/8-inch-11 arbor accepts the full range of 4-1/2-inch accessories
cons: Corded — cord management required on job sites
No kickback protection electronics compared to the Milwaukee 2880-20

picks.name: Milwaukee 2880-20 M18 FUEL Angle Grinder
picks.summary: The 2880-20 is the cordless choice for users who need professional capability away from outlets. Its brushless POWERSTATE motor reaches 8,500 RPM — lower than the corded tools but consistent under load without a cord. RAPIDSTOP brake technology stops the disc in two seconds or less when the paddle is released, which is a meaningful safety feature when changing accessories or working in tight quarters. The electronic clutch KICKBACK BRAKE detects sudden disc binding and shuts off the motor, which the corded options here lack entirely. It accepts both 4-1/2-inch and 5-inch discs.
pros: RAPIDSTOP brake halts disc spin within two seconds — faster than any corded option here
KICKBACK BRAKE electronic clutch detects binding and protects the user
Accepts both 4-1/2-inch and 5-inch discs for more accessory flexibility
Five-year limited tool warranty is the longest in this guide
cons: 8,500 RPM is lower than the 11,000 RPM of the corded tools
At 5.4 lbs bare it is the heaviest tool in the guide
Bare tool only — M18 battery and charger purchased separately

picks.name: Makita GA4534 6-Amp Paddle Grinder
picks.summary: The GA4534 hits 11,000 RPM on a 6-amp motor and weighs just 4.2 lbs — the lightest tool in this guide by 0.4 lbs over the DeWalt. Its machined bevel gears in a metal housing run quieter and smoother than sheet-metal gearboxes, and the paddle switch with lock-off matches the safety standard of the DeWalt and Milwaukee. For users who want the smallest, lightest corded grinder for overhead deburring, tile cutting, or light fabrication, the GA4534 delivers that without sacrificing durability. The trade-off is a 6-amp motor that is slower to recover from heavy disc loading than the 11-amp DeWalt.
pros: 4.2 lbs — the lightest angle grinder in this guide
Machined metal bevel gears run quieter and more smoothly than stamped alternatives
11,000 RPM matches the DeWalt on the same disc diameter
Compact 10-3/8-inch body fits into tighter working positions
cons: 6-amp motor recovers slower from heavy grinding loads than the 11-amp DeWalt
1-year limited warranty is the shortest in the guide
Single disc size (4-1/2 inch only) vs. the Milwaukee's 4-1/2 or 5-inch flexibility

picks.name: Ryobi PCL445B 18V ONE+ Angle Grinder
picks.summary: The PCL445B offers cordless angle grinding at a price that undercuts the Milwaukee 2880-20 significantly, running on the affordable and widely available Ryobi ONE+ 18V platform. Its 9,000 RPM slide switch with lock-on is a familiar control layout, and the three-position adjustable side handle accommodates left- and right-handed use and different grip angles. At 6.18 lbs bare it is the heaviest tool in the guide, which is the main usability limitation. For homeowners who need occasional grinding, cutting tile, or cleaning welds, and who already own Ryobi ONE+ batteries, the value is hard to dispute.
pros: Runs on any Ryobi 18V ONE+ battery — the largest budget cordless platform available
9,000 RPM handles tile cutting, light grinding, and weld-bead cleanup
Three-position adjustable side handle accommodates left or right hand
cons: 6.18 lbs bare is the heaviest tool in this guide
Slide switch with lock-on has slower emergency shutoff than a paddle switch
No electronic brake or kickback protection

faq.q: What is the best angle grinder in 2026?
faq.a: For general-purpose grinding, cutting, and surface prep, the DeWalt DWE402 is the top pick — its 11-amp motor, paddle switch with lock-off, and three-year warranty make it the most well-rounded option. Milwaukee M18 FUEL users should choose the 2880-20 for its RAPIDSTOP brake and KICKBACK BRAKE safety electronics. The Makita GA4534 is the right answer for anyone who prioritizes minimum weight. Budget buyers on the Ryobi ONE+ platform get functional performance from the PCL445B.

faq.q: What is the difference between a paddle switch and a trigger switch on an angle grinder?
faq.a: A paddle switch runs the full length of the handle and releases immediately when your grip changes — the motor stops the moment you lose control of the tool. A trigger switch requires deliberate operation but can be locked on. For grinding and cutting, a paddle switch is considered safer because any accidental drop or loss of grip cuts power automatically. All four tools in this guide use paddle switches.

faq.q: What size angle grinder should I get?
faq.a: Most homeowners and tradespeople use 4-1/2-inch grinders — the size covered by all four tools here. The 4-1/2-inch format handles the widest selection of grinding wheels, cutting discs, flap discs, and wire cups, and the discs are the most affordable and available. Larger 5-inch, 6-inch, and 7-inch grinders remove more material per pass but require more motor power and are heavier. The Milwaukee 2880-20 accepts both 4-1/2-inch and 5-inch discs, which adds flexibility.

faq.q: Is cordless or corded better for an angle grinder?
faq.a: Corded grinders — the DeWalt DWE402 and Makita GA4534 — deliver consistent power without battery swaps, which matters for sustained grinding sessions and heavy fabrication work. Cordless grinders like the Milwaukee 2880-20 and Ryobi PCL445B offer mobility for rooftop flashing, pipe installation, and any application where dragging a cord is impractical. The Milwaukee adds electronic safety features (RAPIDSTOP and KICKBACK BRAKE) that no corded tool in this guide includes.

faq.q: Do angle grinder accessories work across brands?
faq.a: Yes — all four grinders here use a standard 5/8-inch-11 threaded arbor, which accepts any 4-1/2-inch grinding wheel, cutting disc, flap disc, wire cup, or surface-conditioning disc on the market regardless of brand. The Milwaukee 2880-20 also accepts 5-inch accessories. The disc and arbor system is standardized across the industry, so you are not locked into proprietary consumables on any of these tools.

body:
## Angle grinders: one tool, many jobs

Few power tools span as many applications as an angle grinder. With a grinding wheel it shapes and deburrs metal. With a cutting disc it severs rebar, pipe, and tile. With a flap disc it blends welds and prepares surfaces for paint. With a wire cup it strips rust and old coatings. The same four-and-a-half-inch arbor takes all of these accessories, which is why most tool kits include an angle grinder regardless of trade.

The tools in this guide represent four distinct buying scenarios: a corded all-rounder for maximum sustained power, a cordless professional choice with advanced safety electronics, a lightweight corded option for overhead and tight-space work, and a budget cordless for homeowners who already own the platform.

## Safety considerations that affect your choice

Angle grinders are among the most hazardous shop tools. A disc operating at 11,000 RPM contains enough energy to cause serious injury if it shatters or if the tool kicks back on a caught disc. Two features here directly address that risk.

The **paddle switch with safety lock-off** — standard on all four grinders — requires deliberate engagement and cuts power immediately when your hand leaves the handle. This is a significant safety advantage over the older slide-switch or trigger-lock designs common on inexpensive tools.

**Electronic safety systems** in the Milwaukee 2880-20 add a second layer: RAPIDSTOP halts the disc in under two seconds after the paddle is released, and KICKBACK BRAKE detects sudden disc binding and shuts down the motor. These features do not exist on the corded options. If your work involves high-risk situations — overhead cutting, working in confined spaces, cutting brittle tile — the Milwaukee's electronics are worth considering even for buyers who were not initially drawn to it.

## Best overall: DeWalt DWE402

The DWE402 is the clearest recommendation for someone starting fresh or adding a grinder to an existing collection. Its 11-amp motor handles the full range of 4-1/2-inch accessories without complaint — grinding, cutting, and flap disc work — and the paddle switch with lock-off matches the safety expectation of a professional-grade tool. DeWalt's three-year limited warranty with a one-year free service period backs the investment with coverage no other tool in this guide matches except the Milwaukee's five-year tool warranty.

At 4.6 lbs and 12 inches, it is neither the lightest nor the shortest, but the dimensions are proportional to the 11-amp motor, and the tool balances well. For job-site use where an outlet is accessible and sustained output is the priority, the DWE402 is the standard by which the others are compared.

## Best cordless pro: Milwaukee 2880-20

The 2880-20 is for users who need professional grinding capability without a cord and who value the electronic safety package. The RAPIDSTOP brake stops the disc faster than passive deceleration, which reduces the window between tool release and accessory stop — the period when a spinning disc can still cause damage if it contacts something. The KICKBACK BRAKE is a real-world safety differentiator from the corded tools; disc binding that causes kickback is one of the most common grinder incidents.

8,500 RPM is the spec that draws criticism — lower than 11,000 RPM. In practice, a brushless motor maintains RPM more consistently under load than a brushed corded motor losing voltage through a long extension cord. The capability difference is real on sustained heavy grinding but minimal on most common applications. The 5-year tool warranty is the longest in this guide, and the M18 platform's depth means batteries invested here power dozens of other tools.

## Best lightweight corded: Makita GA4534

The GA4534 is the tool for users who spend extended time with a grinder overhead or in awkward positions where every tenth of a pound compounds. At 4.2 lbs it shaves 0.4 lbs off the DeWalt — modest in isolation, meaningful across an eight-hour shift. The machined bevel gears in a metal housing are a refinement that shows up as smoother, quieter operation rather than any spec-sheet metric.

The 6-amp motor limitation is real: it handles deburring, tile cutting, light grinding, and flap-disc work without issue, but sustained heavy grinding on thick steel will stress it faster than the 11-amp DeWalt. For the light-to-medium end of angle grinding tasks, the GA4534 is a compact, well-made choice.

## Best budget cordless: Ryobi PCL445B

The PCL445B answers the question of what a Ryobi ONE+ user gets in an angle grinder. At 9,000 RPM on an 18V platform, it handles the jobs most homeowners actually run: cutting tile, grinding a weld, removing a stripped bolt head, and stripping paint with a wire cup. The adjustable side handle accommodates both right- and left-handed grip orientations, which is a practical detail that some budget tools omit.

The 6.18 lbs bare weight is the clearest limitation — heavier than every other tool in this guide. It is not a tool you want overhead for an hour, but for ground-level and bench work it is manageable. For a homeowner who already owns Ryobi ONE+ batteries and encounters occasional grinding tasks, the PCL445B avoids a separate battery investment while delivering functional performance.
